One such test is simple - just take the first digit of each data number and count how many of each you have. 1 should be most common, 2 somewhat less, etc, following a curve downward. If not, that indicates (though doesn't prove) dirty data.

To see why this would be the case, just consider a set of human weight data in pounds, where a large plurality will contribute 1s because they're between 100-199, with 200-299 decently common, 300+ much rarer, and children contributing a small spread of higher digits due to being 99 or lower.
Pro tip... it still holds true when you switch units as well. Building heights in a city follow this in feet and in meters.
